The **CHA2DS2-VASc** score is a foundational medical risk assessment tool used to evaluate the thromboembolic risk in patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]]. Within the Danish healthcare system, it serves as the primary decision-support mechanism for determining whether a patient has a clinical indication for [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]] [^src17]. The score is deeply integrated into national quality monitoring frameworks, notably forming the "A" (Avoid stroke) component of the [[abc-pathway|ABC Pathway]] for structured atrial fibrillation management [^src8].

### Clinical Guidelines and Quality Indicators
In [[danmark|Denmark]], a CHA2DS2-VASc score of ≥2 is the strict threshold for indicating anticoagulation therapy for both men and women [^src17]. This is because the Danish calculation methodology does not assign points for female sex, making ≥2 the universal cutoff for treatment eligibility [^src1], [^src18], [^src23]. Conversely, patients with a score of <2 do not have an indication for this treatment [^src11], [^src12], [^src24]. 

This threshold directly defines the target populations for several national healthcare quality indicators tracked by the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database]]. For example, the denominator for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]]—which measures the [[ventetid-til-antikoagulations-behandling|waiting time for anticoagulation treatment]]—consists exclusively of incident patients with a score ≥2 [^src9], [^src16], [^src23]. National performance on this indicator is high; 92% of newly diagnosed patients meeting this criteria were started on oral anticoagulation within 30 days of diagnosis [^src17], [^src23]. The score also dictates exclusions and dependencies for other metrics, such as [[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]] (treatment persistence) [^src12], [^src18].

### Epidemiological Distribution
Data from the annual [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark]] reports show the evolving risk profile of the patient population. For incident (newly diagnosed) patients, the average CHA2DS2-VASc score was 1.73 in the 2023 report [^src1], 1.75 in the 2024 report [^src6], and 2.60 in the 2025 report [^src15]. Among prevalent (existing) patients, the average score was 1.47 in 2023 [^src1] and 2.02 in 2025 [^src15]. In the 2024 reporting period, 60.21% of incident patients presented with a score ≥2, thereby qualifying for immediate anticoagulation [^src6].

### Bleeding Risks and Safety Monitoring
While the score is designed to prevent [[iskaemisk-apopleksi|ischemic stroke]] [^src5], [^src21], it is also heavily analyzed in the context of treatment safety and bleeding complications. Paradoxically, a significant proportion of severe bleeding events occur in patients classified as low-risk for thrombosis. Specifically, 43.7% of [[alvorlig-bloedning|severe bleedings]] occurred in patients with a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 0 or 1 [^src4], [^src19], [^src20]. Similarly, 41.1% of [[intrakraniel-bloedning|intracranial bleedings]] happened in patients with a score of 0 or 1 [^src3], and among prevalent patients who suffered an intracranial hemorrhage, 36.7% had a score of exactly 1 [^src21]. These safety outcomes are rigorously monitored under [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] (intracranial bleeding) [^src3] and [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] (severe bleeding) [^src22], highlighting the complex clinical balance between stroke prevention and bleeding risk in atrial fibrillation management.
